name: Month-First Calendar Date

1.definition: Identifies a day by its ordinal position within the named month.
1.details: In June fourteenth, the final numeral identifies the day of the month. The same convention can be written June 14. The month name and day number can do this without an article or a preposition inside the date. A separately formed expression such as the fourteenth of June identifies the same date by a different order and marking.

examples.note: Published example with month followed by an ordinal.
Constructed example in the articleless written format.

relatedConstructions.notes: The two patterns conventionally pick out different calendrical units by number.
The day numeral identifies a position in a conventional system.

grounds.note: Gives Month-plus-Date as a worked example of constructional annotation.

projection.target: A day numeral after a month name is interpreted as an index within that month, with the same interpretation available to ordinal forms and written digits.
projection.evidence: The FrameNet chapter identifies the two slots and their contributions. The restricted month-first pattern leaves other date formats to separate accounts.

curious.title: Dates written month first
curious.summary: A month name followed by a number picks out a day, as in June 14 or November 18.
curious.body:
In June 14th, the number after the month tells you which day of that month is meant. It can be written as a digit, June 14, or as an ordinal, June fourteenth. The date needs no the or of inside it.

The same date can also be said in another order, with extra words: the fourteenth of June. That pattern uses different order and marking. This dictionary describes only the month-first pattern here and leaves other date formats to separate accounts.
curious.try: Write today's date in the month-first way. Then say it again the other way, starting with the number.

teacher.summary: Helps with month-first dates and how the day number relates to the month name.
teacher.explain: A month name followed by a day number identifies a day by its ordinal position within that month. The number can be written as a digit or an ordinal (June 14, June 14th, June fourteenth). No article or preposition appears inside the date. The fourteenth of June identifies the same date with a different order and marking, so teach it as a separate pattern. This dictionary's high-confidence account covers the month-first pattern only. The number works as an index in a conventional system, like the numeral in a numerical label.
teacher.terms: Ordinal number is the traditional term for fourteenth. Month-first is this dictionary's label for the order.

contrasts.note: Month first, with no article or preposition.
The same date with a different order and marking.

watch_for: A learner might read the 14 in June 14 as counting something rather than naming a day.
A learner might add the or of inside a month-first date.
A learner might think June 14 and the fourteenth of June name different days.
teacher.activity: Students write their birthdays in the month-first way, then say them aloud with ordinal numbers. Next they say each birthday in the other order and compare what words changed.

child.hook: Can you say your birthday starting with the month?
child.explain: A month name followed by a number can name a day. June 14th is the fourteenth day of June. You can also say the fourteenth of June.
child.play: Write your birthday starting with the month. Then say it out loud using the number word, like fourteenth. Try a friend's birthday too.
